Should this be handled here or in `SceneTree`? For example here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/741fb8a30687d0662ab6b5c04a2a531440dd29d9/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp#L894-L899

I'm not sure `SceneTree::_main_window_focus_in` might work because it supposedly only checks for the main window focus, while we should check if any of application windows have focus.
`SceneTree::_notification` might work though, because it checks for `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_IN` and `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT` notifications:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/741fb8a30687d0662ab6b5c04a2a531440dd29d9/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp#L901-L923
And also `scene_tree.cpp` already includes the Input header, so that's a plus too:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/741fb8a30687d0662ab6b5c04a2a531440dd29d9/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp#L34

I will change the PR soon and see if this approach works.
Can confirm this approach works too!

While it's nice to have the project setting apply at runtime[^1], I think we should have setter/getter methods in the Input singleton for this:

- `Input.ignore_joypad_on_unfocused_application` property
- `Input.set_ignore_joypad_on_unfocused_application()` method
- `Input.is_ignoring_joypad_on_unfocused_application()` method

This matches how most other input properties are exposed in the Input singleton. Unlike setting/getting project settings from code, typos are caught at compile-time and the API has strong typing.

[^1]: We are currently doing this for some project settings already, but it's pretty inconsistent. This probably needs a proposal and a plan to resolve this, as changing this for existing settings has a small chance of breaking existing projects if they rely on the current behavior.
Done!

The double negative ("ignore" -- "unfocused") makes it harder to understand the meaning of the setting. I would recommend a name such as `accept_joypad_inputs_when_application_unfocused` with the default value `true`.

I tend to disagree, as the action the user would take here is specifically to ignore joypad events on unfocused apps. That's a double negative indeed, but "unfocused app" to me is a well-defined object, so not really a negation per se, if that makes sense. And a setting like "accept" that defaults to true doesn't seem expected to me, if I want to diverge from default behavior, I would expect to enable an option that disables that behavior (so indeed it's enabling a negative option).

But my native language (French) has no issue with double negatives so I may be biased. To me the original setting sounds much clearer than the one you propose, but maybe others would think differently.

Personally, I'm not sure this is a double negative (even though my native language is not English either), I've always thought double negatives are grammar errors and they can be seen in sentences like "I didn't see nothing", "I ain't got no time for that", "But I ain't stupid neither" (Left 4 Dead 2 reference :D), see also https://professorscottsenglish.com/english-grammar/common-grammar-mistakes/double-negatives/why-double-negatives-are-grammatically-incorrect-sometimes/ (I'm not sure how reputable this website is, though)
So basically joypad events should be read when the application is focused, and *ignored* if it's *unfocused*.
It would be double negation if it was "a non-unfocused" for example

I believe that's not enough; as soon as any project setting is changed, the ignore configuration is overwritten again.

Synchronization is missing (input <-> project settings). Or perhaps it would be better to always write/read the project settings and not separate this configuration? Similar use cases must already exist; how are they handled in the engine? Unfortunately, I don't know of a proper solution; I haven't dealt with similar issues before.
